headline: The AI Hype Gap: Adoption Claims Meet Thin Evidence on Campus and in Classrooms
thesis: New data shows higher ed's AI integration is overhyped while EdSurge warns edtech is rushing AI features before proving they work.
summary: Inside Higher Ed reports new usage data showing AI integration in college classrooms is overhyped: the most widely adopted dedicated AI tool, Google Gemini, reached only about 88,000 users across 211 institutions and did not crack the top 100 ed-tech tools. EdSurge's coverage of a new study finds curriculum and edtech providers are bolting AI onto materials with little evidence it improves learning, and EdTech Digest argues AI will work best for the students who need it least. Meanwhile, OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is the first model rated "Critical" for cyber capability, Brookings' task force says AI's risks currently outweigh its benefits for students, and EdTech Week (Oct 14-15, New York) is set to center on higher-ed reinvention and the AI-native talent stack.
